articles.title: These Planets Are Lighter Than Cotton Candy!
articles.summary: Imagine a planet as big as Jupiter but so light it could float in a giant bathtub. Two new “super-puff” worlds, TOI-791 b and c, are even fluffier than cotton candy. They orbit a star 1,110 light-years away.

articles.title: Hawaii's New Roads Are Made from Old Fishing Nets!
articles.summary: Hawaii has a big problem with plastic trash from the ocean. Now, scientists are mixing old fishing nets and plastic bottles into asphalt to build stronger roads. Early tests show the recycled roads don't shed extra microplastics.

articles.title: A Black Hole Might Have Eaten a Star — and We Saw It!
articles.summary: A space telescope called Einstein Probe spotted a super-bright X-ray flash in deep space. Scientists think it was a medium-sized black hole ripping apart and eating a white dwarf star. If true, it's the first time we've ever seen this happen.
